mr_title: feat(@angular-devkit/build-angular): providing a karma config is now optional
mr_description: Karma will now use a builtin config when the `karmaConfig` is not specified.

expected_issues.title: Optional karma dependency imported at module load
expected_issues.description:
karma is an optional peer dependency, but the builder module now imports runtime values (config, constants) from it at top level, so loading @angular-devkit/build-angular without karma installed fails even for unrelated builders.

Previously only types were imported from 'karma' and the module was loaded lazily inside execute(). A value import is emitted as a require() at module load; since the builders are re-exported from the package index, any project that does not install karma (e.g. using Jest or no tests) now crashes on `ng build`. Use `import type` and the lazily loaded karma instance.

expected_issues.title: Built-in config requires every Karma plugin and fails without a clear message
expected_issues.description: When karmaConfig is omitted, the built-in configuration require()s karma-jasmine, karma-chrome-launcher, karma-jasmine-html-reporter and karma-coverage from the workspace. A project missing any of them (for example without coverage) fails with a raw MODULE_NOT_FOUND error instead of a message explaining which plugin is needed or how to provide a karma.conf.js.

expected_issues.title: No test for the built-in Karma configuration path
expected_issues.description: Making karmaConfig optional adds a new default code path (getBuiltInKarmaConfig, coverage folder naming, plugin resolution) and changes the builder schema, but no builder test runs without karmaConfig.
